This course almost succeeded in making me hate biology.  The first few weeks, it's going fine. Just high school biology. And once you let your guard down... Eminem would be pretty silent after taking this course. You hear a million terms each hour of class. Just why? This is an elective course. Just teach general concepts that apply most to our lives. But no, you have to learn the specific terms about every single little thing. The fact that the syllabus is way, WAY too loaded doesn't help either. There is no space to put half the things you see on class to the exams. And how do you justify giving 35 points for the immune system and only 15 for evolution on the final exam, just how? Where is the genetic drift, gene flow, types of natural selection (stabilizing, directional, disruptive), Hardy-Weinberg principal... And they have the audacity to openly say that you are not responsible for what is taught in class, but for the gazillion book chapters. I cannot put the absurdity in words. There is no way in hell I am reading all those pages for an elective course, and there is no way in hell I will remember the specific terms I have heard in this class a month later. So what good is this course to me? I would very much prefer to write a paper for the final that gathers the concepts we have seen in class, or at the very least have an in-class final that requires us to apply the concepts into certain situations. If you are interested in biology and expect to delve deeper into certain concepts, RUN AWAY. Unless you love being a parrot and are willing to sink a thousand hours a week to learn terminology that you will never ever use for the rest of your life, taking this course is gambling. Simply gambling.
